evals.prompt: We are writing Lambda reward functions for `RLVRTrainer` (`Evaluator.create(type="RewardFunction")`) — one for an OSS Qwen model and one for Amazon Nova Lite. An engineer tried using the exact same `lambda_handler(event, context)` return format (`{"statusCode": 200, "body": ...}`) for both, named the evaluator `math-verifier-reward-v1-prod`, made an outbound HTTP call inside the handler, and included zero anti-gaming checks. Fix every bug.
evals.expected_output: Catches all four RLVR invariants: (1) evaluator `name` must match `[a-zA-Z0-9](-*[a-zA-Z0-9]){0,20}` (**max 20 characters** — `math-verifier-reward-v1-prod` is 28 chars and fails!); (2) **OSS vs Nova handler contract split**: OSS parses `event["batch"]`/`body` and returns API-Gateway-style `{"statusCode": 200, "body": json.dumps(results)}`, whereas **Nova** receives a **bare `list`** (`role in ("assistant", "nova_assistant")`, `<|begin_of_solution|>...\boxed{}`) and returns a **bare `list`** of `{id, aggregate_reward_score, metrics_list}`! (3) `< 100 ms` execution, deterministic, bounded `[-1.0, 1.0]`, **zero network calls**; (4) pyramid-layered scoring with **>= 2 anti-gaming checks** (padding, step-skipping, repetition, dummy content, echo attack) tested locally on 4 synthetic cases (`excellent > partial > bad`, `gaming`).
expectations: Activates the finetuning skill

Distinguishes the **OSS RLVR Lambda contract** (`{"statusCode": 200, "body": json.dumps(...)}`) from the **Nova RLVR Lambda contract** (bare `list` input and bare `list` output of `{id, aggregate_reward_score, metrics_list}`)

Catches the `<= 20`-character `Evaluator.create` `name` limit, forbids network calls (`< 100 ms`, bounded `[-1.0, 1.0]`), and requires pyramid scoring + **>= 2 anti-gaming checks** verified across 4 local synthetic test cases
